clue.text: Talkative person in telephone kiosk, say?

definitions.text: Talkative person in telephone kiosk, say?

parts.words: Talkative person in telephone kiosk, say?
parts.note: a phone kiosk is a box where people chatter, and a person who never stops talking gets the same name

explanation.surface: Someone gabbing away endlessly inside a public phone booth.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip who talks incessantly is called this, and a telephone kiosk is jokingly a box for chatter.

clue.text: Top player said to surrender

indicators.note: said tells us to take the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a top player in a tennis tournament is a seed

explanation.surface: A leading sportsman is reported to have given up.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender territory or a point is to yield or give it up.

clue.text: Voice changes a lot

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's voice alters a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The alto is a singing voice range, below soprano.

clue.text: Sign-language policy to change halves

indicators.note: the two halves of the word swap places, the back three letters moving to the front

parts.note: a tactic is a plan or policy for achieving an aim

explanation.surface: A policy for deaf communication is altered halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac is the hand-signal code used by British racecourse bookmakers to pass on odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers' hand signalling is a sign language of its own.

clue.text: Spot start of Chopin piece?

parts.note: a spot of rain is a single drop of rain
a prelude is an introduction or start

explanation.surface: Identify the opening bars of a Chopin composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin's Prelude in D flat, Op 28 No 15, carries this nickname.

clue.text: American dramatist to make a person sick?

parts.note: one is a pronoun meaning a person
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A US playwright whose work makes people feel unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill wrote Long Day's Journey into Night; the apostrophe is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was a Nobel-winning playwright from the United States.

clue.text: Kitty having a good time by day

parts.note: fun means a good time

explanation.surface: A cat enjoying itself on a day out.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pooled stock of money, a fund.

clue.text: A French emaciated ruler, selfish in a way

parts.note: un is French for a
thin means emaciated
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A gaunt French monarch behaves self-centredly.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughtless behaviour, not considering others, is a kind of selfishness.

clue.text: Base to produce electricity on half-tide

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on another, here following it
only the second half of the following word is used

parts.note: to generate is to produce electricity

explanation.surface: A tidal power station works only on half the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes DE, the back half of 'tide'.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and degenerate both mean morally low or corrupt.

clue.text: Police personnel detest vice-spread

indicators.note: spread tells us the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Officers who loathe the spread of vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives are investigating officers in the police force.

clue.text: Sunday day in Germany for men only

parts.note: Tag is the German word for day

explanation.surface: A men-only outing on a Sunday in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party or stag night in Britain is a men-only celebration before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag event admits only male guests.

clue.text: Agent's office making cash profit

parts.note: the post held by a commercial agent who buys and sells for others at a commission

explanation.surface: A broker's position that turns a profit in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a business agent, and the suffix for a post or position gives his office.

clue.text: Arsenal chief a principal herald?

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, the ruler of weapons, as an arsenal is a store of arms
a senior officer of the College of Arms in heraldry

explanation.surface: The head of a football club is also a leading announcer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, a false lead here.
explanation.definitionFit: Garter, Clarenceux and Norroy are the senior heraldic officers bearing this title.

clue.text: Tin and lead, possibly, with unit of luminous intensity

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Metals tin and lead combined with a measure of brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI base unit for how bright a light source is.

clue.text: Channel Islands' seabird in a tank

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, with the possessive S kept
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird from Jersey or Guernsey stuck in a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A water storage tank, as in a loft or toilet.

clue.text: A university assembly, so we hear

parts.note: a rally is a mass assembly

explanation.surface: Reports of a gathering at a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by way of the ears, by listening.

clue.text: Cutting drug given to Olympic finalists

parts.note: acid is slang for the drug LSD

indicators.note: the final letters of the next word, those that finish it

explanation.surface: A drug scandal involving athletes in an Olympic final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalists' takes the last two letters, IC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is sharp and biting, as is an acidic one.

clue.text: Greek satirist's uncial form?

indicators.note: form suggests the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: A classical writer's manuscript in a rounded script.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncial is a rounded capital script used in early manuscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucian of Samosata wrote satirical dialogues in Greek in the second century.

clue.text: Circus performer given Telegraph work, it turns out

indicators.note: turns out signals the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A circus artist is hired by this newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat who balances on a high wire is a big-top act.

clue.text: Get one's act together for famous club

definitions.meaning: to mend one's ways and improve
a London gentlemen's club on Pall Mall

explanation.surface: Advice to shape up, offered at a smart club.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve one's behaviour is to mend one's ways; the Pall Mall club is named after the 1832 Act.

clue.text: Way fleet is brought up to date?

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
RN is the Royal Navy, the British fleet

explanation.surface: How a naval fleet is modernised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something current or contemporary is up to date.

clue.text: For example, earth, energy used in factory

indicators.note: used in places one letter inside another word

parts.note: a plant is a factory
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Soil and power consumed in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one of the bodies orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Taste of pop, long delayed

parts.note: pop and pa are both words for father
late means long delayed

explanation.surface: Soft drink tasted after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Palate is one's sense of taste.

clue.text: Posy arranging, one's happy

indicators.note: arranging means putting the letters in a new order

parts.note: gay in its older sense means happy

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully arranging a small bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bouquet of flowers.

clue.text: Basil, for example, from another border

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plant taken from a neighbouring flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary plant of the kind used for flavouring.

clue.text: Achieved nothing as Queen of Carthage

parts.note: did means achieved
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A queen of ancient Carthage accomplished nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid the Carthaginian queen loved and lost Aeneas.

clue.text: Limits of ambitions

definitions.meaning: the boundaries or extremities of something

explanation.surface: How far one's aspirations can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are both the farthest points and the purposes one aims for.

clue.text: Foreign painter out to achieve eminence

indicators.note: foreign means strange or altered, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: An overseas artist sets out to make a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is renown or high standing, a good name.

clue.text: Defile ticket?

definitions.meaning: a permit giving entry or travel

explanation.surface: Spoiling a ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A defile is a narrow mountain way, and a travel permit has the same name.

clue.text: Penny-pinching, urge non-use of transport

indicators.note: transport means carrying the letters across into a new position

explanation.surface: A miser telling people not to use buses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy and mean with money, not giving freely.
